Action.description: What a requirement does, as a rule matches it.

oneOf.description: Every requirement.
Reading a path, or everything below it.
Writing a path.
Running a command line.

Network access: by any call with the resource `any`, or by one simple command
of a command line that the resource's command pattern matches. A line reaches
the network without a question only when every simple command in it may: by
such a rule, or because only a built-in rule lets it run, as for `tail` in
`npm ci | tail`.

AllowRule.description: One `[[sandbox.allow]]` rule: a kind and a resource, never a command pattern.

oneOf.description:
A `host` exit to one host and port through efr's proxy. It never covers the
whole network, so with `network.mode = "none"` it covers nothing.

host.description:
The host name, matched without case. Never a pattern, an IP address or
`localhost`.

oneOf.description: A contained `write` exit whose bind lies at or below one directory.

project.description:
When set, the rule covers only turns of this project (its root, absolute or
below `~/`).

under.description:
The directory, absolute or below `~/`: the file, the parent dir, the new
file or the new dir that the "yes" opened.

oneOf.description: A `socket` exit to one socket path, never a link.

AnthropicSettings.description: `[anthropic]`: the Anthropic provider, with an API key.

base_url.description: Replaces the Messages API's base URL. Needs a restart.

cache_ttl.description:
How long the prompt cache keeps what a request writes: `auto` is efr's choice,
today everything for an hour, `5m` keeps everything for five minutes, `1h` keeps
everything for an hour. An hour costs more per write and survives a longer
pause. Needs a restart.

models.description:
Models added to the provider's model list, such as a model that the API does
not list yet. A prompt may then name them; their efforts are not checked. An
entry is a model id, or a table `{ id, context_window, max_output_tokens }` that
also gives the model's limits in tokens. A table may name a model of the API's
list to lower its window or its output limit.

workspace_id.description:
The workspace of your API key, sent as the `anthropic-workspace-id` header of
every request. A key that is not scoped to one workspace needs it. Needs a
restart.

AskDestructive.description: When a line of the `auto` mode that deletes or overwrites files asks first.

oneOf.description: Every such line goes to the reviewer or to you.

A line whose files efr's snapshot holds, so `efr undo` can bring them back, runs
at once; the other ones go to the reviewer or to you.
The system bus, `/run/dbus/system_bus_socket`.
The user's session bus, below `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.

BusRule.description:
One `[[dbus.allow]]` entry: more methods of one service on one bus. The entries add
to the defaults and never replace them.

call.description:
The methods, each `IFACE.MEMBER` (at every path) or `IFACE.MEMBER@PATH`, where
PATH may end in `/*` for the path and every path below it.

name.description: The well-known name of the service, such as `org.freedesktop.timedate1`.

CacheMode.description:
How the sandbox treats the tool caches (`~/.cargo`, `~/.cache` and the others of
`sandbox.caches`).

oneOf.description:
An overlay per conversation: the sandbox reads the user's cache and writes to a
private upper layer that the user's own builds never see.
A tmpfs upper layer per call: writes vanish when the call ends.
The caches stay read-only.

CacheTtlChoice.description: How long Anthropic's prompt cache keeps the entries that a request writes.

oneOf.description:
efr's choice, today one hour on every cache entry: an entry for one hour cannot
build on an entry for five minutes, so a mix writes more than it saves.
Five minutes on every cache entry.
One hour on every cache entry.

Check.description:
A check of the words after a [`CommandPattern`](super::CommandPattern)'s `args`.

The enum is deliberately exhaustive, like the other rule types: a new check must be
matched everywhere.

oneOf.description:
`sed` that only prints: `-n` or `--quiet` is given; the only other options are
`-e` and `--expression` with a script, `-E`, `-r`, `-u`, `--regexp-extended`,
`--posix`, `--sandbox` and `--unbuffered`; and each script holds only addresses
(line numbers, `$`, `first~step`, `/regex/` without a bracket expression, and
ranges of them, `addr,+N` and `addr,~N`), `!`, and the commands `p`, `l`, `=`,
`q` and `Q`, separated by `;` or newlines. So no script file (`-f`), no in-place
edit (`-i`), no `w`, `W`, `r`, `R` or `e` command and no `s` command, whose `w`
and `e` flags write a file and run a program.

Every operand is a git ref name, such as `main`, `origin`, `v1.2` or
`feature/x`, and no word is `--`: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`, `~` and
`^`, starting with a letter, a digit or `_`, without `..`, `//` or a trailing
`/` or `.`. So `git checkout -- .`, `git checkout .`, a quoted pathspec such as
`'*'` and a URL such as `https://host/x` fail.

ClassifierSettings.description:
`[classifier]`: who reviews an action that leaves the `auto` sandbox. Every key
applies from the next exit.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort of each review, one lowercase word such as `low`, for the
models that take an effort.

enabled.description:
`true` lets a reviewer model decide most actions that leave the sandbox in
`auto`, and hand the unsure ones to you. `false` asks you about every such
action, as before phase A. Each review is one more request to your provider.

fallback_to_turn_model.description:
`true` lets the turn's model review when the first model is missing, refuses,
times out or gives an answer that does not fit. `false` then asks you.

model.description:
The model that reviews first. Unset: the small model of the turn's provider,
such as `gpt-6-luna` for OpenAI or `claude-haiku-5-5` for Claude.

timeout_secs.description:
How long each model of the chain may take, in seconds, from 1 to 300. A slower
answer goes to the next step.

CommandPattern.description:
A command that a rule names: a program, the words that must follow it, the words
that must not appear, and how many operands it may have.

A pattern judges one simple command at a time. The engine splits a line on `;`,
`&&`, `||`, `|` and newlines, reading quotes as zsh does, and allows a line only
when it allows every simple command in it. A line with a command substitution, a
parameter expansion, a here-document, an output redirection to anything but
`/dev/null`, a group, a background job, an assignment that could change what runs,
or a builtin such as `eval` matches no pattern at all, and falls through to the
rules for every command line. A program that runs commands as another user (`sudo`,
`doas`, `su`, `pkexec`, `run0`) matches no pattern either, even behind a wrapper
such as `env`.

Words are compared after quotes are removed, so `git 'status'` is `git status`. A
command with a pattern outside quotes, such as `src/*.rs`, matches only a pattern
that sets no operand bound, forbids no word without a dash, has no check and no
wildcard alternative without a dash, because zsh replaces the pattern with the
names it matches.

args.description:
The words that must follow the program, in order, such as `["status"]`. A word
may list alternatives separated by `|`, as in `"status|diff|log"`, and an
alternative that ends in `*` matches every word that starts with what comes
before it, as `-Q*` matches `-Qi`. No words matches every invocation.

check.description:
A check of the words after `args` that a list of words cannot express, such as
`sed_print_only` for a `sed` script that only prints. What the check cannot
prove matches nothing.

max_operands.description:
The most operands after the words of `args`. An operand is `-`, a word that
does not start with `-`, or any word after `--`. A value given to an option as a
separate word counts too, so the limit errs towards asking.

max_options.description:
The most options after the words of `args`. An option is a word that starts with
`-`, other than `-` itself, up to and including `--`. With `max_operands`, a
limit of 0 allows the words of `args` and nothing after them, such as `ps -ef`
alone: one more option could make the program read the whole line another way.

min_operands.description:
The fewest operands after the words of `args`, counted like `max_operands`, such
as the unit that `systemctl show` must name, because without one it shows the
service manager's environment.

program.description:
The first word of the simple command, such as `git`. For an `allow` rule, a path
such as `/bin/ls` names a different program. An `ask` or `deny` rule also matches
the base name of a path and the program behind a wrapper such as `env` or `nice`.

under.description:
Where the command must run: a directory or below it (absolute or starting with
`~`), `"project"` for the turn's registered project, or `"scratch"` for the
conversation's `$SCRATCH`. The directory is where the hidden shell is when the
line starts; after a `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` earlier in the line it is unknown,
and the pattern matches nothing.

CompactionSettings.description:
`[compaction]`: when efrd compacts the context of a conversation on its own. Every
key applies from the next turn.

auto.description:
`true` compacts the context on its own when it reaches `auto_at`, before a
model call, and the turn goes on. `false` compacts only when you run `,compact`
(`efr compact`), and a request that does not fit in the model's window fails
the turn with a message that names `,compact`.

auto_at.description:
The percent of the model's context window at which efr compacts on its own,
from 1 to 99. `ctx 100%` in the status row means this point.

ConfigMode.description: A permission mode that `permissions.mode` may name.

oneOf.description: Every call asks, except what your own rules allow.
The built-in rules let commands and files be read with no question. The default.
Shell commands run at once in a kernel sandbox. An action that leaves the sandbox goes to the reviewer or to you. Without the sandbox, a turn runs as `cautious`.

Commands run as you, with no sandbox and no questions. efr still reads each line for a small set of floors (docs/permissions.md, "Full mode"). Valid only with `permissions.allow_full = true`; without it, efrd does not load the file.

ContextSettings.description:
`[context]`: the facts of your terminal that a prompt carries to the model. Every
key applies from the next prompt.

recent_commands.description:
How many of the terminal's recent commands a prompt shows the model, from 0 to
10; 0 shows none. Each one comes with its exit status, its directory when that
is not the current one, and how long ago it ended. The zsh plugin keeps the last
10 command lines of each terminal. It does not keep a `,` line, an `efr` command
or a line that starts with a space.

approval_timeout_secs.description:
Seconds an approval request waits before it expires. Unset: it waits until the
user answers.

draft_interval_ms.description:
The shortest time between two drafts of a running turn, in milliseconds: the
text, the reasoning and the tool input that a terminal shows as they arrive.
Drafts go only to live clients and never into the log; 0 sends every change.

follow_project.description:
A terminal keeps one conversation for each registered project that you worked
in, and one for everything outside projects; a prompt goes to the conversation
of the scope where you send it, and a new terminal picks up the project's
newest conversation that no open terminal holds. false keeps one conversation
per terminal, whatever the scope.

max_queued.description: The most prompts that may wait behind a running turn.

repo_hint.description:
A prompt in a git repository that is not a registered project shows, at most
once a day for each repository, that writes there ask you and how to register
it.

tty_idle_hours.description:
Hours without activity after which a terminal's next `,` line in a scope starts
a new conversation instead of continuing the terminal's conversation of that
scope; 0 continues it forever. Each scope of a terminal has its own clock. A new
terminal picks up a project's newest conversation only when it was active
within these hours.

update_interval_ms.description:
The shortest time between two streamed text updates in the log, in
milliseconds. Live clients see the text sooner, through drafts.

DbusSettings.description:
`[dbus]`: the filtered message bus of the `auto` sandbox. Every key applies from the
next call.

allow.description:
More bus methods that the filter lets through, each a table: `bus` (`system` or
`session`), `name` (the service, such as `org.freedesktop.timedate1`) and `call`
(a list of `IFACE.MEMBER` or `IFACE.MEMBER@PATH`; a PATH may end in `/*`). They
add to the built-in read methods. For systemd, logind, hostnamed, timedated,
localed and timesyncd a method must start with `Get`, `List`, `Can` or `Lookup`.
For other services efr refuses a method that starts with a word that changes the
machine, such as `Start` or `Set`, but it cannot tell every read from a write:
you own each method that you add. Only an editor changes them.

proxy.description:
`true`: in `auto`, the read forms of `systemctl`, `loginctl`, `hostnamectl`,
`timedatectl` and `localectl`, and `notify-send`, run in the sandbox with no
question, through a filtered bus that lets through only a fixed list of methods.
`false`: they need the whole bus, which the reviewer approves for the system bus
and only you for the session bus. efrd turns the filter off when
`xdg-dbus-proxy` is missing or fails its self-test. A change applies to new
calls; a running background job keeps the bus rules of its start.

DiffColors.description: The colours of the lines of a diff: `diff.add`, `diff.remove` and `diff.hunk`.

DiffSettings.description: `[diff]`: how `efr` groups the changed files of a turn. Only `efr` reads it.

groups.description:
Groups of your own for the changed files of a turn: a name, then a list of
globs, such as `evals = ["evals/", "*.eval.toml"]`. `*` matches inside one
part of a path, `**` matches any number of parts, and `?` one character. A glob
without `/` matches the name of a file in any directory; a glob that ends in `/`
matches every file below a directory of that name; other globs match the whole
path from the project root. Your groups match first, in the order of the file,
then the built-in groups: generated, tests, docs, else code. A group named
`code` keeps its files in code; `total` is not a name of a group.

Effect.description:
What happens to a tool call, ordered from the least to the most strict, so the
strictest of several effects is their maximum.

The enum is deliberately exhaustive: the check point in `efr-conversation` must
handle every effect, and a new one must not fall into a wildcard arm.

oneOf.description: The call runs.
The call waits until the user approves or denies it.
The call does not run; the model gets an error that names the reason.

IgnoredFiles.description: Which ignored files a snapshot takes.

oneOf.description: No ignored file.

Ignored files up to 1 MiB each, outside `target`, `node_modules`, `.venv`,
`venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `build`, `.next` and `.cache`, such as `.env`.

JobsSettings.description:
`[jobs]`: whether the model can start background jobs, their limits, and how often
their notices may start a turn. Every key applies from the next job or notice; a job
that runs keeps the limits of its start.

default_minutes.description:
The time limit of a job in minutes when the model names none, from 1 to
`max_minutes`.

enabled.description:
`false`: a shell call with `background: true` fails with a reason, and the model
runs the command in the foreground. Jobs that run go on.

forward_ports.description:
Forward each loopback port that a contained background job listens on to the
same port of 127.0.0.1. A job reads it when it starts. `false` at a reload also
stops the forwards of the jobs that run; a later `true` does not start them
again.

max_minutes.description:
The longest time limit that the model can ask for, in minutes, from 1 to 1440.
A longer one is cut to it.

max_running.description: The most jobs that run at one time in one conversation, from 1 to 64.

max_running_daemon.description: The most jobs that run at one time in all conversations, from 1 to 256.

max_wakes_per_hour.description:
The most turns per hour that job notices start in one conversation, from 0 to
60. 0: a notice never starts a turn; it waits for your next prompt.

max_wakes_per_hour_daemon.description:
The most turns per hour that job notices start in all conversations, from 0 to
120. 0: a notice never starts a turn.

max_wakes_per_watch.description:
The most times that one `watch` pattern of a job can wake the model, from 0 to
10. A higher `max_wakes` of the model is cut to it.

nice.description:
The CPU priority (nice value) of every job, from 0 to 19; 19 is the lowest. A
job never runs at a higher priority than efrd. The disk priority of a job is
always the lowest (the idle class).

anyOf.description: A model id with its limits.

ModelEntry.description: One entry of `[openai] models`: a model id, or a model id with its limits.

ModelLimits.description: A model of `[openai] models` with its limits.

context_window.description:
The model's context window in tokens, from 1000 to 100000000. For a model of the
catalog, it raises or lowers the catalog's window up to the largest window of
the model; above that, efrd uses the largest one and warns once. Unset: the
catalog's window for the model, else a default.

max_output_tokens.description:
The most tokens one model call may produce, from 1 to 1000000. Unset:
`model.max_output_tokens`, else the provider's default.

ModelSettings.description: `[model]`: the provider, the default model of a turn and what each request carries.

effort.description:
The default reasoning effort, such as `low`, `medium` or `high`. Unset: the
provider's default for the model (`medium` for Claude models).

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens one model call may produce. Unset: the provider's default.

name.description:
The default model of a turn, such as `gpt-6.1-sol` or `claude-sonnet-5-5`. Unset:
the default of the provider's model catalog: for OpenAI the model with the best
priority, for Anthropic `claude-opus-5-5` when the API lists it.

provider.description:
The provider of new conversations: `openai-subscription` (the ChatGPT plan),
`openai-api` (an OpenAI API key) or `anthropic-api` (an Anthropic API key). Needs
a restart.

system_prompt.default: You are efr, a coding and system assistant that lives in the user's terminal. The user talks to you from their shell with lines that start with a comma. You run commands in a hidden zsh of your own, which starts in the user's working directory, and you read and write files with your tools. Each prompt starts with a <live_state> block: the state of the user's shell when they sent that prompt. Only the newest block is current; an older one shows the state at its own prompt. The user does not see your tools' output. For each tool call they see one dim line, such as shell: <command>, the last line of its output while it runs, and any approval question or input prompt. Say in your reply what the output showed that matters to them, and never refer to output as "above" or "shown". Every tool call is checked against the user's permission policy and the turn's permission mode, which the live state names: writes outside $SCRATCH may need the user's approval, and secrets are never readable. In the cautious mode, read-only commands such as ls, cat, rg, git status or systemctl status run at once when every argument is written out literally: no $VAR, no $(...), no redirection to a file, no pattern at the start of a word; any other command waits for the user's approval. To change a file, use the edit tool that you have: apply_patch or edit. Do not use sed -i or perl -pi, and do not write a whole file again with write_file for a small change; use write_file only for a new file or a full rewrite. A delete or a move of a file always waits for the user's approval. Prefer small, reversible steps, say what you change, and keep answers short. Put throwaway files in $SCRATCH.
system_prompt.description: The system prompt of every request.

NetworkHost.description:
One `[[network.hosts]]` table: a host that contained commands may reach through the
proxy, with its options.

host.description: The host: a name, `*.suffix`, or an IP address such as `192.168.1.5`.

http.description: Plain HTTP GET and HEAD are allowed too, such as for a mirror.

port.description: The one port that the entry allows. Absent: 443, and also 80 with `http`.

private.description:
The host may resolve to a private address, such as a mirror on your LAN; never
to a loopback, link-local or own address.

NetworkMode.description: What network a contained call has.

oneOf.description: Loopback only (phase 1). A network need is a `host` exit.
TCP through the efr proxy to the hosts of the allow list (phase D).

NetworkSettings.description:
`[network]`: the network of the `auto` sandbox. Every key applies from the next
call.

allow.description:
The hosts that contained commands reach through the proxy on port 443: presets
(`@crates`, `@npm`, `@pypi`, `@go`, `@github-read`, `@pacman-mirrors`), host
names, and `*.suffix` for the names below a suffix of at least two labels. Write
a name in its ASCII (xn--) form. An IP address goes in `[[network.hosts]]`.

deny.description:
Presets, hosts and `*.suffix` entries that no contained command reaches. The
deny list wins over `allow`, `[[network.hosts]]` and every host grant.

hosts.description:
More allowed hosts, each a table: `host` (a name, `*.suffix` or an IP address),
`port` (the one port that the entry allows; absent: 443, and also 80 with
`http`), `http` (plain HTTP GET and HEAD too, such as for a mirror) and `private`
(the host may resolve to an address of your LAN). Only an editor changes them.

max_upload_bytes.description:
The bytes that a contained call may send through the proxy, counted from the
first byte after the CONNECT head; 65536 to 1073741824. A background job counts
for its whole life.

mode.description:
`"proxy"` (the default): contained commands reach the hosts of `allow` through
efr's proxy, and a network need is no review. `"none"`: no network; every network
need is a review that opens the whole network for one call. A change applies to new calls;
a running background job keeps its network until it ends.

netview.description:
`true`: in `auto`, `ss`, the read forms of `ip`, `nstat` and reads of `/proc/net`
run in the sandbox with your machine's network view and no network socket, with
no question. `false`: they go to the reviewer, as a look at the host's network.

api_base_url.description: Replaces the public API's base URL. Needs a restart.

models.description:
Models added to the provider's model list, such as a new model before the
backend lists it. A prompt may then name them; their efforts are not checked. An
entry is a model id, or a table `{ id, context_window, max_output_tokens }` that
also gives the model's limits in tokens. A table may name a model of the catalog
to change its limits: its window up to the largest window that the catalog gives
for the model.

organization.description:
The organization that requests with an API key bill, sent as the
`OpenAI-Organization` header, such as for a key that belongs to several
organizations. Unset: the key's default. Needs a restart.

originator.description:
The `originator` of the subscription login and of every subscription request.
Needs a restart.

project.description:
The project that requests with an API key bill, sent as the `OpenAI-Project`
header. Unset: the key's default. Needs a restart.

subscription_base_url.description: Replaces the subscription backend's base URL. Needs a restart.

websocket.description:
How model calls reach OpenAI: `auto` uses a WebSocket for each model that the
model catalog marks with `prefer_websockets` and HTTP for the other models, `on`
uses a WebSocket for every model, `off` uses HTTP only. A WebSocket stays open for each
conversation, so a call skips the connection setup. A call that the WebSocket
cannot serve goes over HTTP. Needs a restart.

PathClass.description:
Where a path lives, which sets how freely a call may use it.

| Class | Examples | Read | Write |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Scratch` | the conversation's `$SCRATCH` | free | free |
| `UserConfig` | `~/.config`, `~/.zshrc`, other dot entries in `~`, a repository's `.git` in `~` or `$SCRATCH` | free | approval |
| `UserData` | `~/Documents`, `~/p`, `~/.local/share`, `~/.cache` | free | approval, or free inside the turn's registered project |
| `System` | everything outside `~`: `/etc`, `/usr`, `/srv` | free | approval |
| `Secrets` | `~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, password stores, credential files such as `~/.aws/credentials`, the daemon's `secrets/` | denied | denied |

The enum is deliberately exhaustive: a new class must make every consumer decide
what it means, instead of falling into a wildcard arm.

oneOf.description: The conversation's own `$SCRATCH` directory.

The user's configuration: dot entries in `~`, the configured config roots, and
the `.git` of a repository that would otherwise be user data or scratch, whose
config names programs that git runs.
The user's files: everything else in `~`.
Everything outside `~`.
Keys, password stores and credentials. The default policy denies them.

PermissionSettings.description: `[permissions]`: the permission mode, extra secrets and the user's rules.

allow_full.description:
Lets a terminal (`,mode full`), a prompt (`--mode=full`) or `permissions.mode`
choose full mode: commands run as you with no sandbox and no questions. Set it
by hand or with `efr config set`; the settings tool never changes it. It is a
config value, not a lock: a program that can write this file can change it.

mode.description:
The default permission mode of a turn: `manual`, `cautious`, `auto` or `full`. A
prompt may choose another one for its turn. `full` needs
`permissions.allow_full = true`; without it, efrd does not load the file. A turn
from the phone runs with at most `cautious`, and a turn that a job notice starts
with at most `auto`.

rules.description:
The user's rules, `[[permissions.rules]]`, after the built-in rules: the last
rule that matches wins.

secret_paths.description:
Files and directories that count as secrets on top of the built-in ones, so the
model may never read or write them: absolute, or below the home directory as
`~/...`.

Policy.description:
An ordered list of rules in which the last match wins.

Every rule is checked when the policy is built, from code or from the configuration,
so a policy never holds a rule that cannot match.

PresenceSettings.description:
`[presence]`: whether a person is at a conversation to answer its questions. Every
key applies from the next question.

away_after_minutes.description:
The minutes without input in a conversation after which efr counts you away,
from 1 to 1440. Input is a prompt, a steer, an answer or keys for the hidden
shell. `efr away` and `,away` also count you away; your next input ends it.

away_wait_secs.description:
How long a question waits while you are away, in seconds, from 1 to 86400.
Then the call does not run, and the model goes on without it.

push.description:
`true` sends a question that waits while you are away to your paired phones.
No phone client exists yet, so it does nothing today.

Progress.description: When `efr` shows the progress of a turn in the terminal's tab (OSC 9;4).

oneOf.description:
Only in a terminal that is known to draw it: Ghostty 1.2 or later, kitty 0.47
or later, Windows Terminal. Never inside tmux, GNU screen or zellij.
Always, when stdout is a terminal.
Never.

RenderColors.description:
The colour of each role: `[render.colors]` in `config.toml`, `[colors]` in a theme
file. A role that is not set keeps the colour of the layer below it.

accent.description: The spinner and the colour of headings. Unset: slot 3 (yellow).

heading.description: Headings of level 1 and 2. Unset: the accent colour.

muted.description: Notes, tool call lines, labels, rules and the end-of-turn line. Unset: dim.

quote.description: The text of a quote, in italic. Unset: the terminal's foreground.

success.description: Done task boxes and good news. Unset: slot 2 (green).

text.description: Prose and plain lines. Unset: the terminal's foreground.

warning.description: Questions and refusals, in bold. Unset: slot 3 (yellow).

RenderSettings.description:
`[render]`: how `efr` shows replies. Only the client reads it; the daemon accepts it
so one file serves both.

colors.description:
The colour of each role. A role set here wins over the palette file, and the
palette file over the terminal's 16 colours.

motion.description:
Motion in the status row of a running turn: the spinner turns and a band in
the `text` role moves over the state in the `muted` role. `false` shows a still
dot and no band; the time still counts.

palette.description:
A theme file: a `[colors]` table with a colour for each role and, as
`code_theme`, the path of a `.tmTheme` file for code (absolute, `~/...` or
relative to the theme file). `palette` must be an absolute path or start with
`~/`. Unset: no theme file.

progress.description:
The progress bar of the terminal's tab (OSC 9;4) while a turn runs: `auto`
(only in Ghostty 1.2 or later, kitty 0.47 or later and Windows Terminal, never
inside tmux, GNU screen or zellij), `on` or `off`.

theme.description:
The colour theme of code blocks and diffs, such as `catppuccin-mocha`. Unset:
the terminal's own 16 colours. `auto` takes `theme_dark` or `theme_light`, as
the terminal's background is dark or light (`EFR_TERMINAL_BG`). A `code_theme`
in the palette file wins over it.

theme_dark.description:
The theme that `theme = "auto"` takes on a dark background, and when the
background is not known.

theme_light.description: The theme that `theme = "auto"` takes on a light background.

turn_input.description:
An input row below the status row while a turn runs, when the terminal is
interactive. Enter steers the turn, Tab queues a prompt behind it and Esc
interrupts it. `false` shows no input row: keys typed during a turn go to the
shell's next prompt.

turn_summary.description:
One muted line at the end of each turn: how long it took and the tokens it
used, such as `done in 42s, 18.2k tokens in, 1.1k out`.

Resource.description: What a requirement acts on, as a rule matches it.

oneOf.description: Every path, command line and network access.
Every path of one class.

A path and everything below it. It is absolute or starts with `~`, which stands
for the home directory.

Every path inside the root of the turn's registered project: a read of the root
or below it, a write strictly below it. It matches nothing when the scope is not
a registered project, or when that root is `~`, `/` or a directory above `~`.

Every simple command that matches the pattern. With the action `network`, the
network access of such a command; the action `any` does not open the network.

Rule.description:
One rule: when a requirement matches `action` and `resource`, its effect is
`effect`, unless a later rule matches too.

effect.description: The effect when the rule decides.

SandboxSettings.description:
`[sandbox]`: the kernel sandbox of the `auto` mode. Every key applies from the next
call or turn.

allow.description:
Always-allow rules, each a table with a `kind`: `host` (`host`, and `port`,
default 443), `write` (`under`, a directory, and an optional `project`) or
`socket` (`path`). In `auto`, a later exit of that kind and resource runs with
no review and no question, with the same widening that a "yes" gives. The
floors still hold: efrd checks them when it loads a rule, and turns off a rule
that crosses one. Only an editor and the `a` answer of an exit question change
them.

ask_destructive.description:
When a line that deletes or overwrites files asks first: `always`, or
`unless_undoable` (a line whose files efr's snapshot holds runs at once, because
`efr undo` can bring them back).

bwrap.description:
The bubblewrap program, an absolute path. Unset: the first `bwrap` on the
daemon's `PATH`. A change runs the probe again.

cache_days.description:
Days without a call after which a conversation's cache layers are deleted, from 1
to 3650.

cache_max_gib.description:
The size of all cache layers together, in GiB, from 1 to 10000; the oldest
conversation's layers go first.

cache_mode.description:
How the caches are mounted: `overlay` (a private upper layer per conversation),
`tmp` (writes vanish after each call) or `readonly`.

caches.description:
The tool caches that a call reads and writes through a private overlay:
absolute, or `~/...`. A cache that does not exist is skipped.

enabled.description: `false` makes the `auto` mode unavailable: its turns run as `cautious`.

env_deny.description:
More environment variables removed from every call: names, or patterns with
`*`.

env_keep.description:
Variables that the scrub of secret-like names keeps: names, or patterns with
`*`.

export_deny.description: More names that never return to the hidden shell: names, or patterns with `*`.

keep_downloads.description:
In the `tmp` cache mode, the download caches (`~/.cargo`, `~/go/pkg/mod`,
`~/.npm`, the bun and pnpm stores) keep what a call downloads for the rest of
the conversation, in efr's private layer, as the `overlay` mode does. The other
caches stay `tmp`. Off by default: each call then takes about 3 to 4 ms more,
above the launch gate of 10 ms.

mask.description:
More paths that a call reads as empty: absolute, or `~/...`. In `auto`, a
`read_file` of them asks.

mask_globs.description:
Names masked inside each write root, to depth 3: `*` matches any text, and a
leading `!` keeps a name readable.

offline_hints.description:
Tell package managers to work offline while the sandbox has no network
(`CARGO_NET_OFFLINE`, `npm_config_offline`, `UV_OFFLINE`, `GOPROXY=off`).

promote_env.description:
The exported variables that return from a call to the hidden shell: names, or
patterns with `*`. A name of the built-in never list never returns.

protect.description: More paths that stay read-only even inside a write root: absolute, or `~/...`.

rebuildable.description:
Directory names whose deletion is not destructive, because builds make them
again.

surface_files.description:
The files that run code later outside the sandbox: names or paths relative to a
write root, with `*`. The end of an `auto` turn lists the ones it changed.

synced_dirs.description:
Folders that a sync service copies off the machine: absolute, or `~/...`. A write
to them is an exit that only you can approve.

write_projects.description:
Which registered projects a call may write: `turn` (the turn's project), `named`
(also the registered projects that the command names) or `all`.

write_roots.description:
More write roots for every call: absolute, or below the home directory as
`~/...`. Floors still apply inside them. The home directory itself is refused.

ScreenChoice.description: Which screen backend the hidden shells get.

oneOf.description: ghostty when this build has it, otherwise vt100.
The Zig-free vt100 backend.
The libghostty-vt backend.

ShellSettings.description: `[shell]`: how hidden shells start and when idle ones stop.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes without output or input, at a prompt and unwatched, before a hidden
shell is closed; 0 keeps idle shells.

interactive_timeout_minutes.description:
The longest a command runs before its call answers the model, in minutes, while
a terminal that can type answers follows the conversation. It applies to a
command outside the sandbox that may ask at the terminal (`sudo`, `ssh`, `rsync`
or `git` over ssh), also when the reviewer, a rule or full mode allowed it, and to
any command that waits for input when its timeout passes. A command that still
runs in the hidden shell after its call answered, and waits for input, stops at
this limit. The model's own timeout holds when no such terminal follows. Read at
each call.

login.description: Start the hidden shell as a login shell.

program.description: The shell, an absolute path. Unset: `zsh` on the `PATH`.

sudo_cache.description:
`keep` leaves sudo's credential cache to sudo; `per_call` makes the hidden shell
forget sudo's and doas's credentials after each call, before anything else runs
there. Read at each call.

SnapshotSettings.description:
`[snapshot]`: the snapshots before and after each call that can write, in the turn's
registered project, `$SCRATCH` and, in `auto`, the registered projects that a line
names. Every key applies from the next call.

enabled.description:
`false` takes no snapshot: a `shell` call and the end of a turn then list no
changed files, and `efr diff` has nothing new. A file tool still shows its diff.

home_max_files.description:
The most files of one directory that efr copies before a call can write all of
it, outside the project and `$SCRATCH`, from 0 to 100000. A larger directory
gets no copy, and the end of the turn says so.

home_max_mib.description:
The most MiB of one directory that efr copies before a call can write all of
it, outside the project and `$SCRATCH`, from 0 to 16384. A larger directory gets
no copy, and the end of the turn says so.

ignored.description:
Which ignored files a snapshot takes: `none` or `small` (up to 1 MiB each,
outside build and dependency directories, such as `.env`).

keep_turns.description:
The turns of each conversation whose snapshots stay, newest first, from 1 to
10000; older ones are deleted.

max_age_days.description:
Days without a snapshot after which the store of a project or `$SCRATCH` is
deleted, from 1 to 3650.

max_file_mib.description:
Files above this size in MiB are left out of a snapshot, from 1 to 1024: a new
untracked file, and a file that grows past it, which then shows as changed with
no line counts.

max_files.description:
A project or `$SCRATCH` with more files than this is not snapshotted, from 100 to
1000000; the debug log says so, and efr counts its files again after 10
minutes.

mirror_max_mib.description:
The most MiB of a project's git objects that efr copies into its store once per
turn, so `efr undo` can move the project's branches and tags back, from 0 to
65536; also the most that one turn's copy may add. 0 copies none: undo then
restores files but no refs. A store keeps at most 4 times this in copies.

SudoCache.description:
What a hidden shell does with sudo's cached credentials after a call that ran sudo
or doas.

oneOf.description: sudo's own cache stays, for as long as sudoers keeps it (5 minutes by default).

The hidden shell forgets the credentials after each call (`sudo -k`, `doas -L`),
so the next sudo asks for the password again.

Under.description:
Where a command must run for a [`CommandPattern`] to match it: below a directory,
in the turn's registered project, or in the conversation's `$SCRATCH`.

In the configuration it is one string: `"project"`, `"scratch"`, or a directory that
is absolute or starts with `~`.

UndoSettings.description:
`[undo]`: whether `efr undo` can take back a turn. The snapshots themselves are in
`[snapshot]`. Every key applies from the next call or undo.

enabled.description:
`false` turns undo off: `efr undo` refuses, the end of a turn shows no undo
hint, and in `auto` a line that deletes or overwrites files goes to the reviewer
or to you, as with `sandbox.ask_destructive = "always"`.

WebSocketChoice.description: Whether model calls go over the Responses WebSocket transport.

oneOf.description:
Follow the model: a model that prefers WebSockets uses one, any other model
uses HTTP.
Every model uses a WebSocket.
Every model uses HTTP.

WriteProjects.description: Which registered projects a call of the `auto` mode may write.

oneOf.description: The turn's project only.
The turn's project and the registered projects that the command names.
Every registered project.

description:
The effective settings: the built-in defaults, then `config.toml`, then whatever
environment variables and flags the program applies with
[`apply_override`](Self::apply_override).

A missing file is an empty one, so every value is its default. The fields are
public so a test can start from [`Settings::default`] and change what it needs; a
changed field keeps the source it had.

classifier.description: The reviewer model that decides most actions that leave the `auto` sandbox.

compaction.description: When efrd compacts a conversation's context on its own.

context.description: What a prompt tells the model about your terminal: its recent commands.

dbus.description: The filtered message bus of the `auto` mode.

diff.description: How `efr` groups the changed files of a turn.

jobs.description:
Background jobs: whether the model can start them, their limits, and how often
their notices may start a turn.

log.description:
The tracing filter of the daemon, in `EnvFilter` syntax, such as `info` or
`info,efr_=debug`.

default.system_prompt: You are efr, a coding and system assistant that lives in the user's terminal. The user talks to you from their shell with lines that start with a comma. You run commands in a hidden zsh of your own, which starts in the user's working directory, and you read and write files with your tools. Each prompt starts with a <live_state> block: the state of the user's shell when they sent that prompt. Only the newest block is current; an older one shows the state at its own prompt. The user does not see your tools' output. For each tool call they see one dim line, such as shell: <command>, the last line of its output while it runs, and any approval question or input prompt. Say in your reply what the output showed that matters to them, and never refer to output as "above" or "shown". Every tool call is checked against the user's permission policy and the turn's permission mode, which the live state names: writes outside $SCRATCH may need the user's approval, and secrets are never readable. In the cautious mode, read-only commands such as ls, cat, rg, git status or systemctl status run at once when every argument is written out literally: no $VAR, no $(...), no redirection to a file, no pattern at the start of a word; any other command waits for the user's approval. To change a file, use the edit tool that you have: apply_patch or edit. Do not use sed -i or perl -pi, and do not write a whole file again with write_file for a small change; use write_file only for a new file or a full rewrite. A delete or a move of a file always waits for the user's approval. Prefer small, reversible steps, say what you change, and keep answers short. Put throwaway files in $SCRATCH.

model.description: The provider, the default model of a turn and what each request carries.

network.description: What network a contained call of the `auto` mode sees.

permissions.description: The permission mode, extra secrets and the user's rules.

presence.description:
When efr counts you away from a conversation, and how long a question waits
then.

sandbox.description: The kernel sandbox of the `auto` mode.

screen.description:
The screen backend of the hidden shells: `auto`, `vt100` or `ghostty`. Needs a
restart.

shell.description: How hidden shells start and when idle ones stop.

snapshot.description: efr's own snapshots, which show what a call and a turn changed in files.

undo.description: `efr undo`, which takes back the changes of a turn from efr's snapshots.
